args.title: BestTime carries out its actions
args.description:
The application calls these methods on BestTime by exactly these names and keyword arguments. Each one changes the object as described.
- Field `difficulty_id` holds exactly one of: "beginner" (Best time for Beginner); "intermediate" (Best time for Intermediate); "expert" (Best time for Expert)
args.given_when_then: Given a BestTime in a state where the action is allowed (arrange that by setting its fields). When a BestTime is created with only its required fields and nothing is called on it Then Constructed with id, difficulty_id (beginner, intermediate or expert), game_id, best_seconds and achieved_at from the first win of that difficulty; it holds exactly those values, with events empty. When `record_win(game_id, difficulty_id, elapsed_seconds, achieved_at)` is called with valid values Then Applied automatically when a game is Won. For a standard difficulty (beginner, intermediate, expert) where elapsed_seconds < best_seconds, best_seconds becomes elapsed_seconds and game_id and achieved_at are updated; a slower or equal time keeps the stored best. A custom difficulty, or a difficulty_id differing from this record's, changes nothing, and the object's fields show it afterwards. One test function per method.

kwargs.interface_contract:
- Action `record_win`: params [`game_id`, `difficulty_id`, `elapsed_seconds`, `achieved_at`] — Applied automatically when a game is Won. For a standard difficulty (beginner, intermediate, expert) where elapsed_seconds < best_seconds, best_seconds becomes elapsed_seconds and game_id and achieved_at are updated; a slower or equal time keeps the stored best. A custom difficulty, or a difficulty_id differing from this record's, changes nothing.
- A newly created `BestTime` (constructed with only its required fields) holds: Constructed with id, difficulty_id (beginner, intermediate or expert), game_id, best_seconds and achieved_at from the first win of that difficulty; it holds exactly those values, with events empty.
- Field `difficulty_id` holds exactly one of: "beginner" (Best time for Beginner); "intermediate" (Best time for Intermediate); "expert" (Best time for Expert)
kwargs.other_rules:
- New best time: Given a stored best time of B seconds for a standard difficulty When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds with T < B Then the best time becomes T for that difficulty on this device
- First win sets best time: Given no best time stored for a standard difficulty When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds Then a best time of T is recorded for that difficulty
- Slower or equal win keeps best: Given a stored best time of B seconds for a standard difficulty When the player wins in T seconds with T >= B Then the best time remains B
- Custom games record no best time: Given a game on Custom difficulty When the player wins it Then no best time is created or changed
- Lost or abandoned games record no best time: Given a game that ends Lost or Abandoned When it ends Then no best time is created or changed
- Best time shown per standard difficulty: Given best times stored on this device When the player views best times Then the fastest win for Beginner, Intermediate and Expert is shown, and Custom has no entry

import pytest

from src.domain.best_time import BestTime


ACHIEVED_FIRST = "2024-01-10T09:00:00+00:00"
ACHIEVED_LATER = "2024-02-20T18:30:00+00:00"


def _make(difficulty_id, best_seconds=100):
    return BestTime(
        id="bt-1",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="game-first",
        best_seconds=best_seconds,
        achieved_at=ACHIEVED_FIRST,
    )


@pytest.mark.parametrize("difficulty_id", ["beginner", "intermediate", "expert"])
def test_new_best_time_holds_exactly_constructed_values(difficulty_id):
    bt = BestTime(
        id="bt-1",
        difficulty_id=difficulty_id,
        game_id="game-first",
        best_seconds=100,
        achieved_at=ACHIEVED_FIRST,
    )

    # Constructed from the first win: the values passed in are kept as-is.
    assert bt.id == "bt-1"
    assert bt.difficulty_id == difficulty_id
    assert bt.game_id == "game-first"
    assert bt.best_seconds == 100
    assert bt.achieved_at == ACHIEVED_FIRST
    # Nothing has been called, so no events were raised.
    assert bt.events == []


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "record_difficulty, win_difficulty, elapsed, expect_update",
    [
        # Standard difficulty, faster by one second (just inside the < boundary): update.
        ("beginner", "beginner", 99, True),
        # Same rule for another standard difficulty (each kind is covered).
        ("expert", "expert", 99, True),
        ("intermediate", "intermediate", 99, True),
        # Equal time (exactly at the boundary): elapsed < best is false, best kept.
        ("beginner", "beginner", 100, False),
        ("expert", "expert", 100, False),
        # Slower time: best kept.
        ("beginner", "beginner", 101, False),
        # Custom difficulty with a faster time: changes nothing.
        ("beginner", "custom", 99, False),
        # Different standard difficulty with a faster time: changes nothing.
        ("beginner", "intermediate", 99, False),
    ],
)
def test_record_win(record_difficulty, win_difficulty, elapsed, expect_update):
    # Given: a stored best of 100 seconds from game-first at ACHIEVED_FIRST.
    bt = _make(record_difficulty, best_seconds=100)

    # When
    bt.record_win(
        game_id="game-second",
        difficulty_id=win_difficulty,
        elapsed_seconds=elapsed,
        achieved_at=ACHIEVED_LATER,
    )

    # Identity and difficulty of the record never change.
    assert bt.id == "bt-1"
    assert bt.difficulty_id == record_difficulty

    if expect_update:
        # Same standard difficulty and 99 < 100: best becomes 99,
        # game_id and achieved_at come from the new win.
        assert bt.best_seconds == elapsed
        assert bt.game_id == "game-second"
        assert bt.achieved_at == ACHIEVED_LATER
    else:
        # Either elapsed >= 100, or the win's difficulty is custom / differs
        # from this record's: the stored best from game-first stays.
        assert bt.best_seconds == 100
        assert bt.game_id == "game-first"
        assert bt.achieved_at == ACHIEVED_FIRST
